newsitem.title: UK: French Connection to expand chain.
newsitem.headline: French Connection to expand chain.

text.p: Retail and wholesale and fashion clothing firm French Connection Group Plc plans to expand its retail chain strength to over 50 shops from a current 43 and boost its product range in 1997/98, its chairman said.
"The new stores would be in the U.K. and in the U.S.," David Bernstein, French Connection's chairman told Reuters.
The group currently has 30 shops in the U.K. and 13 in the United States.
Bernstein said the firm would also introduce more products that would be compatible with its existing clothing range.

Earlier on Thursday, French Connection made a positive forecast of its performance for the year to January 1997 saying its pretax profits would be above market expectations and in the region of six million stg.
"We are pleased with the trading performance in the second half and particularly the contribution made by our retail division," Bernstein said in a statement.
"Our turnover was 83 million stg," he said.
French Connection reported a turnover of 71 million stg in the previous year. Its like-for-like sales for the year at both French Connection and Nicole Farhi outlets rose by over 20 percent, it said.
Bernstein said the firm did especially well in its lycra items, both clothing and underwear.
The company reported pretax profits of 3.43 million stg for the year to January 31, 1996. It will announce its January 1997 results in April.
Bernstein said shareholders could expect a growth of more than 10 percent in dividend payout on shares.
The company paid two pence per share dividend in the previous year. It has already paid a 0.5 pence/share interim dividend in the current year.
Shares in the company was marked 40 1/2 pence higher at 310 pence.
